title: UI prescription-verification set (XOLAIR only — only ready indexed label)
note: Other Medcare labels (Lucentis/Ocrevus/Rozlytrek/Avastin) are uploaded but still processing with 0 chunks; not used. Excludes Avastin example and prior sample/PV wording.

questions.question: A 35-year-old with chronic spontaneous urticaria who remains symptomatic on an H1 antihistamine was prescribed XOLAIR 150 mg subcutaneously every 2 weeks. Does the XOLAIR prescribing information recommend every-2-week dosing for CSU? State the label frequency.
questions.expected: Does not match. For CSU, label recommends 150 mg or 300 mg SC every 4 weeks (not every 2 weeks).

questions.question: A 4-year-old with moderate persistent asthma inadequately controlled on inhaled corticosteroids was prescribed XOLAIR. Does the asthma indication in the XOLAIR label cover a 4-year-old?
questions.expected: Does not match. Asthma indication is for adults and pediatric patients 6 years of age and older.

questions.question: For IgE-mediated food allergy, a clinician plans to give XOLAIR 300 mg as a slow intravenous infusion every 4 weeks. Does that route match the prescribing information?
questions.expected: Does not match. XOLAIR is for subcutaneous administration only.

questions.question: A patient in status asthmaticus was prescribed XOLAIR to treat the acute episode. Is XOLAIR indicated for status asthmaticus or acute bronchospasm according to the label?
questions.expected: No. Limitations of Use: not indicated for acute bronchospasm or status asthmaticus.

questions.question: An adult with chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps who had an inadequate response to nasal corticosteroids is being considered for XOLAIR as add-on maintenance. Is that use consistent with the labeled indication?
questions.expected: Yes. CRSwNP in adults ≥18 with inadequate response to nasal corticosteroids, as add-on maintenance treatment.

questions.question: What is the recommended dosage range and schedule for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) in the XOLAIR prescribing information?
questions.expected: 75 mg to 600 mg by subcutaneous injection every 2 or 4 weeks based on pretreatment serum total IgE and body weight (Table 3).

questions.question: According to the boxed WARNING, can anaphylaxis to XOLAIR occur only with the first dose, or can it also occur later during treatment?
questions.expected: Anaphylaxis has occurred after the first dose and also beyond 1 year after beginning treatment. Initiate in a healthcare setting and observe patients.

questions.question: Before considering patient self-administration of XOLAIR with a prefilled syringe or autoinjector, how many doses should the patient receive under healthcare-provider guidance with no hypersensitivity reactions?
questions.expected: At least 3 doses under healthcare-provider guidance with no hypersensitivity reactions (among other selection criteria).

questions.question: For chronic spontaneous urticaria, should the XOLAIR dose be calculated from serum total IgE and body weight the same way as for asthma?
questions.expected: No. CSU dosing is not dependent on serum IgE (free or total) level or body weight; use 150 mg or 300 mg SC every 4 weeks.

questions.question: In which patients is XOLAIR contraindicated according to the prescribing information?
questions.expected: Contraindicated in patients with severe hypersensitivity reaction to XOLAIR or any ingredient of XOLAIR.

questions.question: What does the XOLAIR Drug Interactions section say about formal drug interaction studies?
questions.expected: No formal drug interaction studies have been performed with XOLAIR.

questions.question: A patient with IgE-mediated food allergy was told XOLAIR can replace strict food allergen avoidance and can be used as emergency treatment for anaphylaxis after accidental exposure. Does that advice match the label?
questions.expected: Does not match. Label: use in conjunction with food allergen avoidance; not indicated for emergency treatment of allergic reactions, including anaphylaxis.

questions.question: What monitoring precaution does the label give for patients at high risk of geohelminth (parasitic) infection while on XOLAIR?
questions.expected: Monitor patients at high risk of geohelminth infection while on XOLAIR therapy.

questions.question: An adult with asthma was prescribed XOLAIR 375 mg by mouth once daily. Does this regimen match the asthma dosing in the prescribing information?
questions.expected: Does not match. Asthma dose is 75–375 mg by subcutaneous injection every 2 or 4 weeks based on IgE and weight — not oral daily.
